```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}

#using copilot to generate a ggplt scatter plot using penguins dataset
#plot bill_length_mm on the x-axis and bill_depth_mm on the y-axis
#colour points by species and use geom_point with size 3
#add minimal theme and clean labels

plot <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Bill Length vs Bill Depth in Penguins",
       x = "Bill Length (mm)",
       y = "Bill Depth (mm)",
       color = "Species")

plot

```

```{r}
#generate a boxplot comparing flipper_length_mm across different species, faceted by island, using custom colour palettes 

plot2 <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ island) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Adelie" = "#1f77b4", "Chinstrap" = "#ff7f0e", "Gentoo" = "#2ca02c")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Flipper Length by Species and Island",
       x = "Species",
       y = "Flipper Length (mm)",
       fill = "Species")

plot2
```

```{r}
penguins
#generate a smooth line plot of the penguins data set 
#x-axis is body mass and y-axis is bill length, colour lines by species 
#include the range of standard error 
#add theme classic and clean labels 

plot3 <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Bill Length vs Body Mass in Penguins",
       x = "Body Mass (g)",
       y = "Bill Length (mm)",
       color = "Species")
plot3

```

```{r}
#using if else with tidyverse
# Sample coral data
coral_monitoring <- tibble(
  site = c("Site_A", "Site_B", "Site_C"),
  depth_m = c(12, 35, 8)
)

# Classify depth using if_else
coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>% 
  mutate(zone = if_else(depth_m > 30, "Deep Reef", "Shallow Reef"))

#using mutate - used to create, modify or delete columns in a dataset 
coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>% 
  mutate(reef_category = case_when(
    depth_m < 10  ~ "Lagoon / Flats",
    depth_m <= 30 ~ "Crest / Slope",
    depth_m > 30  ~ "Mesophotic / Deep",
    TRUE          ~ "Unclassified" # Catch-all remainder
  ))

#write an R script that initialises a tibble named marine_stations containing a column for salinity with values 35, 28, 32, and 12. 
#Use the pipe operator (%>%) and mutate() combined with case_when() to create a new column named environment_type. 
#Classify values below 15 as "Estuarine", values between 15 and 30 as "Brackish", and values above 30 as "Marine".
marine_stations <- tibble(
  salinity = c(35, 28, 32, 12)
) %>%
  mutate(environment_type = case_when(
    salinity < 15 ~ "Estuarine",
    salinity >= 15 & salinity <= 30 ~ "Brackish",
    salinity > 30 ~ "Marine"
  ))
marine_stations
```

```{r}
# Function Definition
calculate_coral_mortality <- function(initial_count, surviving_count) {
  
  # Logic safety switch using our conditional tools!
  if (initial_count <= 0) {
    stop("Initial count must be greater than zero.")
  }
  
  mortality_rate <- (initial_count - surviving_count) / initial_count
  return(mortality_rate)
}

# Utilizing your custom function
calculate_coral_mortality(initial_count = 120, surviving_count = 84)


#Custom function to convert celsius to fahrenheit that has a conditional safety check using an if statement that halts exeution via stop() f the entered value s below absolute zero(-273.15 degrees Celsius)
convert_temp_c_to_f <- function(celsius) {
  if (celsius < -273.15) {
    stop("Temperature below absolute zero is not physically possible.")
  }
  fahrenheit <- (celsius * 9/5) + 32
  return(fahrenheit)
}
#testing the convert_tempt_c_to_f function with a valid value and an invalid value 
convert_temp_c_to_f(25) #valid inpt
convert_temp_c_to_f(-300)  # This will trigger the stop() condition


```
